en: [172] It is established;
indeed, such is the nature of those born of the body.
Indeed, for those born of a body, such is the case here; it is not otherwise for men dwelling in the next world.
Nor is it otherwise for men, according to the power of the sūtras.
The sacred thread does not come from the womb of a Śūdra woman; indeed,
it does not come from within the womb.
Having performed the funeral rites for him,
who had emerged from the womb together with an infant,
this indeed is his [final act].
Having performed this consecration,
it was indeed placed upon his neck for the sake of the name of the twice-born.
It was placed upon his neck for the sake of the name of the twice-born.
Twice-bornness is one,
which is innate by nature; twice-bornness is another, which arises from the thread of consecration.
Furthermore, from the *Sanskārasūtra*,
for the sake of mocking all the twice-born,
[he composed] everything for the sake of mocking all the twice-born.
Oh, how strange is the disposition of those who are deluded!
Oh, how strange is the disposition of those who are deluded!
Another wandering mendicant, with the perception that it was green, [cut off a blade of grass].
Another wandering mendicant, with the notion that they are made of earth,
takes up even staffs made of wood;
he takes up even staffs made of wood.
At the end of the nights of the winter season and so forth, he performs his ablutions in the water while trembling. [285]
He performs his ablutions in the water, his body trembling as it is afflicted by the cold,
his body trembling as it is afflicted by the cold.
How can there be meditation here,
or how can there be the recitation of excellent mantras,
when a most wicked serpent has entered the house?
When an extremely wicked serpent has entered the house,
who here in this blinding darkness would be free from anxiety?
Who here in this blinding darkness would be free from anxiety?
Body, speech, and mind constitute the triple-staff;
body, speech, and mind constitute the triple-staff; the mind alone, which is the essence of all, constitutes the single-staff.
[173v = 31v] *Ekaka*°: The concentration of the mind (*cittasya samādhāna*) is the single-staffed form of the illustrious Brahmā, infinite and singular.
The staff-bearer assumes the single, infinite form of the illustrious Brahmā;
the staff-bearer does not enter into the water. [287] The staff-bearer does not enter into the water.
Saila, whose body was once smeared with ashes,
became again a devotee of Śiva with his limbs covered in ashes; at the conclusion of his bath, he perceived him as the lordly elephant among elephants.
At the conclusion of his bath, the one with the intellect of a lordly elephant,
constantly bearing a mass of matted hair for the sake of happiness,
constantly bore a mass of matted hair for the sake of happiness.
One worships a mere stone with favorite flowers;
yet another, moreover, wears a shaven head and carries a skull-bowl.
Another, moreover, wears a shaven head and carries a skull-bowl,
having placed ornaments of human bone upon his body.
Having placed ornaments of human bone upon his body.
For the sake of glorious accomplishment, he wanders in the cremation ground; for the sake of glorious accomplishment, he wanders in the cremation ground.
How can there be accomplishment through ignorance for one of such evil intellect? [289]
How can there be accomplishment for one of evil intellect through ignorance?
There is the Kālāmukha, the Pāśupata, and likewise another.
The Kālāmukha, the Pāśupata, and likewise another.
Naked, with very long matted hair,
and wearing a girdle of muñja grass.
Wandering for alms, they go toward death;
wandering for alms, they go toward death.
They desire to proceed toward peace.
They do not proceed to the state of liberation that has been accomplished.
[290] They do not proceed to the state of liberation that has been accomplished.
Tib. thar pa’i go ’phang grub nas ’gro bar ’gyur ba ma yin no.
Another, moreover, was naked with shorn hair;
another, moreover, was naked with shorn hair, smeared all over his body and teeth with filth.
Smeared with filth from head to foot,
afflicted by hunger and thirst, the one of evil intellect perishes;
the one of evil intellect, tormented by hunger and thirst, becomes bound.
There is never any proceeding upon the path to liberation;
furthermore, another [type of practitioner] dwells at the foot of trees during the rainy season.
Furthermore, another [ascetic] dwells at the foot of a tree during the rainy season, and practices exposure to the heat during the summer and spring seasons.
He practices exposure to the heat during the summer and spring seasons.
In the winter season, the one who dwells in the open air practices in the open air; for the sake of the ultimate truth, he undergoes extreme hardship. [292]
One undergoes hardship for the sake of the ultimate truth;
"a naked man on a lion-throne" is improper—
“a naked man on a lion-throne” is improper.
And this parasol was torn away by me.
